note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names. Empty fields (track, code, level, description) are filled; authored transfer_check values replace ONLY the two known generic placeholder sentences — real source checks are never overwritten (guard in tools/normalize_blocks.py). v0.83.0 — every theme now carries `bands`, so the fill-empty path writes five authored sentences per theme (the same mechanism used for the community packs) instead of the shared sentence with its band suffix.
credential_correction: Credential correction (v0.52.0, proposed — not yet adopted by the review board): the v0.1.0 import named these tracks' credential with the bare band level 'Practitioner'. The `credential` on each track below replaces that level word only (real credential names are never overwritten); tools/normalize_blocks.py applies it as the one deliberate, counted exception to fill-empty-only and prints the count. Names follow the packs' own shape — a person and a capability, never a level word, never a job title the credential cannot confer.

bands.9–10: Arrange real respite care for yourself or a family carer, on your own.
bands.11–12: Help a family find and arrange real respite care.

themes.theme: Caring for somebody who does not want it (CR)
themes.description: Refusal, pride and risk — caring within another adult's right to decide, and when safety overrides.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play care within refusal: the person's right to decide respected, the safety line named, the compromise found.

bands.K–2: Be patient if someone doesn't want help right away, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Explain why someone might resist help even when they need it, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Navigate a real situation where care is resisted, respectfully, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Provide real care respectfully to someone who resists it, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through the real, hard work of caring for a resistant person.

themes.description: What dying looks like, what comfort care does, and being present in the last days without panic.
themes.transfer_check: Describe what dying commonly looks like and demonstrate two comfort measures, staying present through a role-played hour.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult a question if you're wondering about someone very sick.
bands.3–5: Learn that some illnesses mean a person is nearing the end of life, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Understand real end-of-life care basics and what comfort means, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Support a real family member through end-of-life care, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through the real practical and emotional work of end-of-life care.

themes.description: The first week's duties — certification, notification, the funeral — and the support for the person left.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the first-week checklist — certification, notifications, the funeral, the person left — for a case-study death, in order.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult how you feel if someone you love has died.
bands.3–5: Name a feeling you have after a loss and tell a trusted adult, with help.
bands.6–8: Recognise real grief responses in yourself or family after a death, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Handle the real practical steps that follow a death, on your own.
bands.11–12: Support a family through the real practical and emotional steps after a death.

themes.description: Paid care as skilled work — the training, the standards and the routes into it locally.
themes.transfer_check: Map the real local routes into paid care work — training, certification, starting pay — from actual providers.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what a person who helps sick people does at work.
bands.3–5: Name one job where people help care for others, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real paid care role and what it involves, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real paid care job as a possible path, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else what real professional care work actually involves.

themes.description: The carer's own health, network and plan — kept deliberately, because the caring depends on it.
themes.transfer_check: Write your own or a case-study carer's support plan — health, network, backup — and activate one element of it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who helps the grown-up who helps everyone else.
bands.3–5: Name one way a tired carer can get support, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real support resource for family carers, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Seek out real support for yourself as a carer, on your own.
bands.11–12: Connect a real carer to the support resources they need.
